resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2015 review says most lookouts are staffed through the core fire season and the rest only during high hazard. A government bears page says each site is staffed by a lookout observer, generally from April to October. Neither is specific to Berland, so the story reports both and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only page that names this tower is its OpenStreetMap node, which carries tags for name, lattice construction and observation use, but no date, height, operator or status. The brief's 'built 2015', 30 m height and 'closed' access come from Alberta's lookout dataset, which was read only at metadata level (no per-site values), and no source read supports them, so none is used. The 2015 review and the bears page describe the whole Alberta network and are used only as context; the story says so. The two accounts of staffing differ (most lookouts staffed through the core season versus each site staffed generally April to October), and the story does not pick one for this tower. Two WebSearch calls found no Berland-specific news, heritage or agency page. Before publishing, look for an Alberta Wildfire statement or a local source on the Berland tower's construction and status; the story is short because the evidence is short.
